sections.h2: How fast can a Valley Stream house sell?
sections.html:
Anywhere from a few weeks to several months, and the route you choose decides which. Nassau County village owners generally compare three paths: hiring an agent, selling alone, or accepting a cash offer on the house in its current condition.

With homes averaging above $600,000, most buyers borrow, and the lender's appraisal and underwriting dictate when closing can happen. A cash buyer needs neither. Any path involves village, county and state paperwork, covered below.

sections.h2: Valley Stream housing at a glance
sections.html:
Valley Stream is a village of homeowners, with some of the higher housing costs on Long Island's western edge. Nearly four in five homes are owner-occupied.

Valley Stream housing and population
MeasureValley Stream
Residents, 2025 estimate40,379
Households12,340
Owners among occupants78.7%
Typical home value$616,100
Typical monthly rent$2,124
Household income at the midpoint$133,190

A building boom that began in 1922 took the village from 11,790 residents in 1930 to more than 38,000 by 1960, so many houses are old and have been renovated more than once. That makes permit history matter later in a sale.

sections.h2: Which school district serves your address
sections.html:
The answer changes by street. Valley Stream elementary districts 13, 24 and 30 cover most of the village and feed the Valley Stream Central High School District. A few southern blocks go to the Hewlett-Woodmere Union Free School District instead.

Schools are usually a buyer's first question, so check your address and name the district in the ad. That choice also determines the school tax bill the buyer inherits, and school taxes go to the Town of Hempstead, not the village.

The village Building Department reviews construction plans, issues permits, and applies the state building and fire codes alongside the village code. Permits are required for:

  • Finished basements and cellars, interior alterations, additions and dormers.
  • New or replacement windows, siding, exterior painting, driveways, steps and patios.
  • All plumbing and electrical work, including direct replacement of fixtures.
  • Pools, hot tubs, fences, solar panels and changes in use or occupancy.

A building permit expires 12 months after issue. An unpermitted basement left by a prior owner tends to surface in the buyer's attorney review, so call the department and learn what records exist for your parcel before listing. Buyers of older homes may also ask about the village Private Sewer Lateral Repair Program.

sections.h2: Parking and trash rules buyers ask about
sections.html:
Buyers new to the village tend to ask about parking and trash. The village answers both.

  • No parking on village streets overnight between 3:30 a.m. and 5:30 a.m.; the Clerk's Department issues temporary permits for overnight guests.
  • Garbage can be set out after 6 p.m. the evening before pickup; the weekly cap is 250 pounds and pails may not exceed 32 gallons.
  • Recycling takes #1 and #2 plastics and plain brown corrugated cardboard.
  • Construction debris can go to the village sanitation yard for $120 a ton, payable by check.

A full house cleanout will blow past 250 pounds quickly, so plan on the sanitation yard or a hauler.

sections.h2: Village tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
The village taxes about 11,000 parcels and runs its own Tax Department. Village tax comes due June 1, with no penalty through July 1. Later payment brings 5 percent for the first month and another 1 percent each month after. Partial payments are refused, and balances still unpaid go to the annual lien sale on the first Tuesday in May.

On a sale, whatever village tax is still owed gets paid out of closing proceeds. Request a written payoff from the Tax Department so your attorney has an exact figure.

The village reports an equalization rate of .87 and a residential assessment ratio of .90. Its assessment roll is final on April 1. The grievance period opens February 1 and closes the third Tuesday of February, which is Grievance Night, held 4 to 8 p.m. A denied complaint can go to a Small Claims petition, for which the Nassau County case number is obtained from April 1 through May 1.

  • Seniors 65 and over with household income under $28,900 can apply for a village exemption.
  • Military service earns 15 percent for wartime service plus 10 percent for combat-zone service, and Cold War service earns 10 percent.
  • Firefighters with more than five years of service receive 10 percent.

The senior, disability and firefighter filing window is September 1 through December 31 every year, so it is open now. STAR goes through the Nassau County Department of Assessment.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Nassau County
sections.html:
The Nassau County Clerk in Mineola records every Valley Stream deed. Submit the TP-584 transfer tax form and the RP-5217 transfer report along with it, plus the IT-2663 estimated income tax form if the seller lives out of state. Transfer and mortgage tax must be paid by certified check.

Deeds get bounced here for small errors. Put the section, block and lot on page one, use a street address rather than a post office box, and sign everything in original ink. Delivery to the clerk should happen an hour or more ahead of closing, or use an approved e-recording company.

State transfer tax is $2 per $500 of price. The 1 percent buyer's tax applies to residences of $1 million or more, which is well above the village median. After closing, the new owner must send the village Tax Department a written request with the deed and the section, block and lot to change the owner and mailing address.

With a cash purchase there is no appraisal, no underwriting and no mortgage contingency, so closing is not held up waiting on a bank. The house is bought in its current condition, which spares you permit chases, repairs and a cleanout.

Government paperwork does not go away. Tax payoffs, deed forms and county recording all still apply, so pull together your latest village tax bill, permit records and current deed early. Your attorney can then order the payoff and fill out the TP-584 and RP-5217 right away.

A simple order of work: confirm your school district, ask the Building Department about permits, request the tax payoff, then hand the deed details to your attorney. Doing the first two before you accept an offer keeps surprises out of the contract period. Keep copies of everything you send, since the village and the county each keep their own files.

faqs.q: Do village taxes in Valley Stream have to be paid at closing?
faqs.a: Any unpaid village tax is normally settled at closing. Ask the village Tax Department for a payoff, since the village bills once a year on June 1 and accepts no partial payments.

faqs.q: How expensive are homes in Valley Stream?
faqs.a: The typical owner-occupied home is $616,100. About 78.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied and the median gross rent is $2,124.

faqs.q: When can I challenge my Valley Stream assessment?
faqs.a: File between February 1 and the third Tuesday of February, when Grievance Night runs from 4 to 8 p.m. The village roll is final on April 1, and denied complaints can move to a Small Claims petition.

faqs.q: Does Valley Stream require a permit for a finished basement?
faqs.a: Yes. The Building Department lists finished basements and cellars among the projects that need a permit. Ask what is on file for your address before you list, because missing permits surface during a buyer's inspection.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed for a Valley Stream sale?
faqs.a: The Nassau County Clerk records it. The clerk requires the TP-584 and RP-5217 forms, certified checks for transfer tax, and the section, block and lot on the first page.
